page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position this instance in the lower tiers of modern cloud compute offerings. In CPU testing, the Intel Xeon 8163 processor achieves a single-core Geekbench score of 987.0 and a multi-core score of 2173.0, while stress-ng multi-core performance reaches 2934.5. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached large-block read speeds dropping to 20.58 GB/sec and a Passmark memory score of 1246.19, both placing in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Cryptographic and vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AES are present, but overall execution speeds remain modest.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.xlarge offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a lower entry point than newer-generation instances, though its resource density and performance-per-resource are constrained. It is best suited for lightweight compute-focused workloads that do not require high memory capacity or rapid I/O. Appropriate use cases include basic web serving, where it achieves a static throughput of 3.36 GB/sec, lightweight Redis caching delivering 2.86 million SET operations per second, and minor background processing tasks.
